design.decision: A nil bidder dumps a dangerous off-suit honor instead of following with a card that might win; the covering partner trumps with a high [♠] whenever it wants, even while holding the led suit.
design.opponent: Revealed the first time an honor is played off suit; opponents can no longer bust a nil by leading into a suit the nil bidder holds only high cards in.
design.rationale: One rule helps two plans in opposite ways: shedding honors protects a nil, and free high trumps protect a big contract, so it is worth buying before you know your build. Free-play rules measured poorly at common (the AI may misuse them), so this tests the broadest version at the rarity where a strong rule change belongs.
design.draftText: Your team can play [J]s through [A]s even when it can follow suit

critic.concerns: Near-duplicate of rb-honors-free (range only); keep one. Free [J]-[A] of [♠] overlaps uc-trump-freely.
